     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiFiniteness
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.MulEquiv
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The χ-ledger: `chi_step`, `chi_divisorSheaf`, and Riemann–Roch-lite
    11	
    12	The Euler-characteristic ledger for divisor sheaves on the curve bundle `X` (integral,
    13	smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a field `K`, with finite `H⁰` and
    14	`H¹` of the structure sheaf — the two instance hypotheses through which properness enters):
    15	
    16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_skyModule`: `χ(sky_x M) = dim_K M` — the skyscraper contribution.
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_step` (★ ledger keystone): the one-point dévissage step
    18	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D − x)) + [κ(x) : K]`, from the additivity of `χ` along the dévissage
    19	  short exact sequence `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky_x J → 0` and `dim_K J = residueDeg x`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf` (★ ledger keystone): the closed ledger
    21	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`, by dévissage induction from `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.deg_divOf`: principal divisors have degree zero — transport `χ`
    23	  along the multiplication isomorphism `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪(0 − div g)` and cancel in the ledger.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.riemann_inequality` (G9): `deg D + χ(𝒪_X) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))`.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_nsmul_point_unbounded` (G9): `h⁰(𝒪(n·x))` is unbounded in `n`,
    26	  for any closed point `x` — no rational point is needed, only `residueDeg x ≥ 1`.
    27	
    28	All statements are phrased against the one-point divisor `CurveDivisor.single hx 1`
    29	(definitionally the dévissage twist: `devissageDivisor_eq_sub`).
    30	-/
    31	
    32	set_option autoImplicit false
    33	
    34	universe u
    35	
    36	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    37	
    38	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    39	
    40	open Scheme
    41	
    42	/-! ## The skyscraper contribution -/
    43	
    44	section Skyscraper
    45	
    46	variable {K : Type u} [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    47	
    48	/-- `h⁰` of a skyscraper sheaf is the dimension of its value module. -/
    49	theorem h0_skyModule (x : X) (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) :
    50	    Sheaf.h0 (skyModule x M) = Module.finrank K M :=
    51	  (skyModuleGammaEquiv x M).finrank_eq
    52	
    53	/-- **The Euler characteristic of a skyscraper** is the dimension of its value module:
    54	`h¹` vanishes and `h⁰` is computed by `skyModuleGammaEquiv`. -/
    55	theorem chi_skyModule [Nontrivial K] (x : X) (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) :
    56	    Sheaf.chi (skyModule x M) = Module.finrank K M := by
    57	  rw [Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 (skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x M), h0_skyModule]
    58	
    59	end Skyscraper
    60	
    61	/-! ## The ledger -/
    62	
    63	section Ledger
    64	
    65	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    66	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    67	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    69	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    70	
    71	/-- **The dévissage step of the χ-ledger** (★): subtracting a closed point `x` from the
    72	divisor drops the Euler characteristic by the residue degree `[κ(x) : K]`:
    73	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D − x)) + residueDeg x`. The divisor `D − CurveDivisor.single hx 1` is
    74	definitionally the dévissage twist `devissageDivisor hx D` of the landed short exact
    75	sequence (`devissageDivisor_eq_sub`). -/
    76	theorem chi_step {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    77	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
    78	      Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + X.residueDeg K x := by
    79	  have hS := devissageSES_shortExact K hx D
    80	  -- the five finiteness inputs and the `H¹(sky) = 0` input, in the `devissageSES` spelling
    81	  haveI h₁0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 0) :=
    82	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero K (devissageDivisor hx D)
    83	  haveI h₁1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
    84	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (devissageDivisor hx D)
    85	  haveI h₂0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 0) :=
    86	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero K D
    87	  haveI h₂1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 1) :=
    88	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K D
    89	  haveI h₃0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 0) :=
    90	    haveI := moduleFinite_jumpModule K hx D
    91	    moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_zero x (jumpModule K hx D)
    92	  haveI h₃1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
    93	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
    94	  have hadd := Sheaf.chi_eq_add_of_shortExact hS
    95	  -- identify the three χ's with their divisor-sheaf/skyscraper spellings (definitional)
    96	  have hX₂ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ = Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) := rfl
    97	  have hX₁ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ =
    98	      Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := rfl
    99	  have hX₃ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ = (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
   100	    have h := chi_skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)
   101	    rw [finrank_jumpModule K hx D] at h
   102	    exact h
   103	  rw [hX₂, hX₁, hX₃] at hadd
   104	  exact hadd
   105	
   106	/-- **The χ-ledger, closed** (★): for every Weil divisor `D` on the curve bundle,
   107	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`. Base case `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X`, step `chi_step`, glue
   108	`CurveDivisor.induction_devissage`. -/
   109	theorem chi_divisorSheaf (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   110	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
   111	      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
   112	  refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.induction_devissage
   113	    (P := fun D => Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
   114	      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D)
   115	    ?_ (fun {x} hx D => ?_) D
   116	  · rw [Sheaf.chi_congr (divisorSheafZeroIso K), CurveDivisor.deg_zero, add_zero]
   117	  · rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D]
   118	    have hstep := chi_step K hx D
   119	    have hdeg := deg_devissageDivisor K hx D
   120	    rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D] at hdeg
   121	    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
   122	
   123	/-- **Principal divisors have degree zero**: `deg (div g) = 0` for a unit `g` of the
   124	function field. Multiplication by `g` identifies `𝒪(0)` with `𝒪(0 − div g)`
   125	(`mulEquivDivisorSheaf`), so the two sides of the χ-ledger force the degrees to agree. -/
   126	theorem deg_divOf (g : X.functionFieldˣ) :
   127	    CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) = 0 := by
   128	  have hcongr := Sheaf.chi_congr (mulEquivDivisorSheaf K g (0 : X.CurveDivisor))
   129	  rw [chi_divisorSheaf K (0 : X.CurveDivisor),
   130	    chi_divisorSheaf K ((0 : X.CurveDivisor) - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g),
   131	    CurveDivisor.deg_zero, zero_sub, CurveDivisor.deg_neg] at hcongr
   132	  omega
   133	
   134	/-- **The Riemann inequality** (G9, general conditional form): for every Weil divisor `D`,
   135	`deg D + χ(𝒪_X) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))` — from the χ-ledger and `h¹ ≥ 0`. The curve-level
   136	`deg D + 1 − genus` form is derived in `ChiCurve`. -/
   137	theorem riemann_inequality (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   138	    CurveDivisor.deg K D + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
   139	      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
   140	  have h := chi_divisorSheaf K D
   141	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
   142	    rw [Sheaf.chi]
   143	    omega
   144	  omega
   145	
   146	/-- **Unbounded growth of `h⁰` along multiples of a point** (G9): for every closed point
   147	`x` and every bound `N` there is `n` with `N ≤ h⁰(𝒪(n · x))`. No rational point is
   148	needed: `residueDeg x ≥ 1` suffices. -/
   149	theorem h0_nsmul_point_unbounded {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (N : ℕ) :
   150	    ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
   151	  have key : ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
   152	      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
   153	    intro n
   154	    have hchi := chi_divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   155	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n,
   156	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx (n : ℤ)] at hchi
   157	    have hchile : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) ≤
   158	        (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
   159	      rw [Sheaf.chi]
   160	      omega
   161	    have hres : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
   162	      exact_mod_cast Scheme.residueDeg_pos hx
   163	    have hmul : (n : ℤ) * 1 ≤ (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) :=
   164	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hres (by positivity)
   165	    have hchiO : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) =
   166	        (Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) := rfl
   167	    -- `hchi` rewrote the divisor to `single hx n`; transport back is definitional
   168	    have hchi' : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) =
   169	        Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
   170	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n]
   171	      exact hchi
   172	    omega
   173	  refine ⟨N + Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K), ?_⟩
   174	  have h := key (N + Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K))
   175	  omega
   176	
   177	end Ledger
   178	
   179	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **Hartshorne II.6.1**: for a nonzero rational function `f` on a Noetherian
integral scheme `X` satisfying `(*)`, the order function `Y ↦ ord_Y(f)` is
nonzero at only finitely many prime divisors `Y`. This is the well-definedness
side condition for `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal`.

The proof uses a finite affine cover and the fact that only finitely many
height-one primes can divide the numerator or denominator on each chart.

The statement is generic in `f` (no `f ≠ 0` hypothesis is threaded): on
`f = 0` the function `Y ↦ ord_Y(0) = WithZero.log 0 = 0` has empty support,
which is finite, so the conclusion holds vacuously. -/
theorem rationalMap_order_finite_support {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    (f : X.functionField) :
    (Function.support (fun Y : X.PrimeDivisor =>
      Scheme.RationalMap.order Y f)).Finite := by
  -- Case 1 (f = 0): the order function evaluates to
  -- `WithZero.log (Ring.ordFrac _ 0) = WithZero.log 0 = 0` at every
  -- prime divisor, so the support is empty (finite vacuously).
  by_cases hf : f = 0
  · subst hf
    convert Set.finite_empty
    ext Y
    simp only [Function.mem_support, ne_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false,
      Decidable.not_not, Scheme.RationalMap.order_zero]
  -- Case 2 (f ≠ 0): Stacks 02RV. Global Noetherian = quasi-compact gives a
  -- FINITE affine cover `X = ⋃ᵢ Uᵢ`; every prime divisor's generic point lies in
  -- some `Uᵢ`, so the support is contained in the finite union of the per-chart
  -- supports, each finite by `finite_chart_support` (the affine-chart
  -- minimal-primes core).  Without `[CompactSpace X]` (equivalently
  -- `[IsNoetherian X]`) this fails: the line with infinitely many origins is a
  -- non-quasi-compact counterexample.
  · haveI : CompactSpace X := inferInstance
    set 𝒰 := X.affineCover.finiteSubcover with h𝒰
    refine Set.Finite.subset (Set.finite_iUnion fun i : 𝒰.I₀ =>
      finite_chart_support (isAffineOpen_opensRange (𝒰.f i)) hf) ?_
    intro Y hY
    refine Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨𝒰.idx Y.point, ?_, hY⟩
    exact 𝒰.covers Y.point

/-! ## §3. Divisor of a closed point on a curve

On a smooth proper curve `C` over a field, every closed point `P ∈ C` is a prime
divisor (it is closed, integral, of codimension one in the one-dimensional integral
scheme `C`). The associated Weil divisor is `[P] = 1 · P ∈ Div(C)`. -/

/-- **The Weil divisor associated to a closed point `P` on a curve.** The element
`[P] := 1 · P ∈ Div(C)`, i.e. the prime divisor `P` with multiplicity one.

For a smooth proper curve every closed point is automatically a prime divisor (it
is a codimension-one integral closed subscheme of the one-dimensional integral
scheme `C`); conversely every prime divisor on a curve is of this form, so an
arbitrary divisor on `C` is a finite formal `ℤ`-linear combination
`Σ nᵢ · [Pᵢ]` of closed points.

Blueprint reference: `def:divisor_closed_point` (Hartshorne II §6 p. 137).

The definition is zero outside its intended codimension-one scope. It
case-splits on `Order.coheight P = 1` (the codimension-one witness of
`PrimeDivisor`). On the branch where the equality holds — automatic for a
closed point on a one-dimensional integral scheme — we promote `P` to a
`PrimeDivisor` via the witness and return `Finsupp.single ⟨P, h⟩ 1`, i.e.
the prime divisor `P` with multiplicity one. On the off-branch (junk regime)
we return the zero divisor; see `ofClosedPoint_eq_single` for the equation in
the codimension-one regime. -/
noncomputable def ofClosedPoint {C : Scheme.{u}} (P : C)
    (_hP : IsClosed ({P} : Set C)) : C.WeilDivisor :=
  if h : Order.coheight P = 1 then Finsupp.single ⟨P, h⟩ 1 else 0

/-- In the hypothesised regime where the closed point `P` has coheight one
(the codim-1 condition automatic for a closed point of a one-dimensional
integral scheme), `ofClosedPoint P hP` is the prime divisor `P` with
multiplicity one. -/
lemma ofClosedPoint_eq_single {C : Scheme.{u}} (P : C)
    (hP : IsClosed ({P} : Set C)) (h : Order.coheight P = 1) :
    ofClosedPoint P hP = Finsupp.single ⟨P, h⟩ 1 := by
  simp [ofClosedPoint, h]

/-- Off-branch: outside the codim-1 regime, `ofClosedPoint` is junk-defined as
the zero divisor. (Only relevant when the user supplies a "closed point" that
does not have coheight one in the ambient scheme — e.g. a generic point or a
codim-≥2 point on a higher-dimensional scheme.) -/
lemma ofClosedPoint_eq_zero {C : Scheme.{u}} (P : C)
    (hP : IsClosed ({P} : Set C)) (h : Order.coheight P ≠ 1) :
    ofClosedPoint P hP = 0 := by
  simp [ofClosedPoint, h]

/-! ## §4. Degree of a divisor over an algebraically closed base -/

/-- **Degree of a Weil divisor on a smooth proper curve over `k̄`.**

Over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, every closed point of a smooth proper
curve `C` has residue field `k̄`, so each prime divisor `[P]` contributes degree
one to the sum, and `deg(D) := Σᵢ nᵢ` is the sum of the integer coefficients of
the formal sum `D = Σ nᵢ · [Pᵢ]`.

(Over a general field `k` one weights by the residue-field degrees
`Σᵢ nᵢ · [κ(Pᵢ) : k]` to recover the geometric degree; the project's RR bridge
needs only the `k̄` specialisation.)

Blueprint reference: `def:divisor_degree` (Hartshorne II §6 p. 137; Stacks 0BE0).

Implementation: `Finsupp.sum D (fun _ n => n)` is the sum of all coefficients of
the finitely supported function representing `D`. -/
noncomputable def degree (D : X.WeilDivisor) : ℤ :=
  (D : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ).sum (fun _ n => n)

/-- **The degree map is a group homomorphism `Div(C) → ℤ`.**

`deg(D₁ + D₂) = deg(D₁) + deg(D₂)`, `deg(-D) = -deg(D)`, `deg(0) = 0`. Bundled
as an `AddMonoidHom` for downstream use (the linear-equivalence quotient
`Cl(C) := Div(C) / im(div)` will inherit a `deg : Cl(C) → ℤ` from this).

Blueprint reference: `thm:divisor_degree_hom` (immediate from `def:divisor_degree`).

Implementation: built from `Finsupp.liftAddHom (fun _ ↦ AddMonoidHom.id ℤ)`, the
generic Mathlib packaging that lifts a family of `AddMonoidHom`s indexed by the
support into a single `AddMonoidHom` on the finsupp. Unfolds to
`D.sum (fun _ z ↦ z) = degree D` (see `degree_hom_apply` below). -/
noncomputable def degree_hom : X.WeilDivisor →+ ℤ :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom (fun _ ↦ AddMonoidHom.id ℤ)

@[simp]
lemma degree_hom_apply (D : X.WeilDivisor) : degree_hom D = degree D :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom_apply (α := X.PrimeDivisor) (M := ℤ) (N := ℤ)
    (fun _ ↦ AddMonoidHom.id ℤ) D

/-- **Degree of the zero divisor is zero.** A direct consequence of
`degree_hom` being an `AddMonoidHom`. -/
@[simp]
lemma degree_zero : degree (0 : X.WeilDivisor) = 0 := by
  rw [← degree_hom_apply]; exact map_zero _

    80	theorem chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}

   151	  toFun L := classDegFun K L
   152	  map_zero' := classDegFun_one K
   153	  map_add' L L' := classDegFun_mul K L L'

   156	Weil divisor `D` is `deg D`, for *every* `D`. -/

   162	the degrees, `classDeg (L · L') = classDeg L + classDeg L'`. Immediate from `map_add` of the

   164	theorem classDeg_mul (L L' : X.CechPic) :

   166	  classDegFun_mul K L L'

   195	theorem classDeg_divisorClass (D : X.CurveDivisor) :

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FGAPicRepresentability
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GeometricallyConnectedSection
import AlgebraicJacobian.Genus

/-!
# The identity component of the Picard scheme

Let `G` be a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type. Its **identity
component** `G⁰` is the connected component of `|G|` containing the image of
the identity section. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of `G`, of
finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`, and its formation
commutes with extension of the base field (Kleiman, §5, Lem.~`lem:agps`).

This file develops that substrate for an arbitrary `k`-group scheme (§1) and
then specialises it to `G = Pic_{C/k}`, the Picard scheme of a smooth proper
geometrically integral curve `C/k` (§2), obtaining `Pic⁰_{C/k}` together with
the degree map `Pic_{C/k}(k) → ℤ` (§3) whose kernel it cuts out on
`k`-points (§4). For `C` of positive genus, `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the Jacobian
variety of `C`.

## Main results

- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` — the identity component
  `G⁰` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of finite type, as a `k`-scheme (an
  object of `Over (Spec k)`): the open subscheme of `G` carried by the
  connected component of the image of the identity section.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme` —
  the inclusion `G⁰ ↪ G` is both an open and a closed immersion.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` —

/-!
# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the residue-weighted degree and the section-drop bounds

This file supplies two further legs of the campaign's cluster P
(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`, P3/P4):

* the **residue-weighted (adelic) degree** `deg_k D = Σ_P D(P)·[κ(P):k]`, which is
  the degree the χ-ledger actually telescopes to (the geometric
  `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` is its specialisation at residue degree one, i.e.
  over an algebraically closed base field);
* the **section-drop bounds** `ℓ(D) ≤ ℓ(D + P) ≤ ℓ(D) + [κ(P):k]`;
* **residue-degree positivity** `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]` and its consequence that a nonzero
  effective divisor has *positive* weighted degree.

The drop bounds are **unconditional** — they need neither the ledger's
connecting/surjectivity data nor the strong-approximation input, only the
finite-dimensionality instances.  The `≤` direction of the one-point step is
`localStep_finrank_le` (node N14, already landed) read through the rank–nullity
identity `finrank_localStepDom`; that is precisely the observation that the
*upper* bound of the χ-ledger does not need the residue map to be onto.

## Statements whose ledger input is explicit

The results that genuinely need the closed ledger `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` take it
as an explicit hypothesis `hledger`, in the same style as the existing
`Adelic.riemann_inequality`.  Nothing here introduces a new gate class, and no
statement is left as a `sorry`.  Under that hypothesis this file derives:

* `degK_principal_eq_zero` — **principal divisors have residue-weighted degree
  zero**, from the class-invariance of `χ` (`ClassInvariance.lean`).  This is the
  adelic form of the open geometric leaf
  `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`.
* `degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one` and
  `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` — the collapse to the
  **unweighted** degree when every residue degree is one, and the resulting
  unweighted principal-degree-zero statement.  Together these reduce the open leaf
  to the single residue-field fact `[κ(P):k̄] = 1` plus instance plumbing; §4
  records why the `sorry` is nonetheless left in place.
* `ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg` — `deg_k D < 0 ⟹ ℓ(D) = 0` (campaign P4(a)).
* `degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell` — the Riemann inequality in closed weighted form.

## What is NOT proved here (read this before consuming)

Three distinct gaps in the vanishing story are kept apart deliberately:

1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → h¹(D) = 0`, for
   one fixed base field `k`.  Not proved here and not derivable from the ledger
   alone: it needs a base vanishing `h¹(𝒪(n₀·x₀)) = 0` plus surjectivity of
   `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` (the "peel an effective divisor" step).  The sibling project
   proves its analogue (`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean`) from an
   FLV-class machine that has no AJC counterpart.
2. **Extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
   Strictly more than (1): it needs flat base change of the bound along
   `k → κ`.  Nothing in this file quantifies over extensions.  The predicate itself is written
   down as `Adelic.UniformlyBoundedVanishing` (`Adelic/ResidueField.lean` §5), so this gap is
   statable and open rather than unformulable.
3. **Global generation** — `𝒪(D)` generated by global sections above the bound.
   Strictly more than (1): it needs `h¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed point, i.e. the
   bound raised by the maximum residue degree.  Not addressed *in this file*, but
   proved in `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` from the same inputs as (1); it is the
   equality case of this file's own drop bound `ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg`.  It is
   **not** more than (2): global generation and extension uniformity are independent,
   and (2) remains open.

## Provenance

The residue-weighted degree, the drop bound and the `deg < 0 ⟹ ℓ = 0` corollary
are **rederived in the AJC adelic abstractions**; they are not ports.  The
sibling `AJCR RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean` / `Degree.lean` prove related
statements on the `CurveDivisor`/`divisorSheaf` substrate, whose names do not
exist in this project.  The argument reused from AJCR is the χ-transport step of
`deg_divOf`; its AJC counterpart is `chi_eq_of_principal_shift`.
-/

`κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P`, realised as a `k`-subquotient of `K(X)`; its `k`-dimension is the

function `t` with `ord_P t = 1 - m` (which exists by `exists_order_eq` — the
intrinsic uniformizer-power order, *no* distinguished global uniformizer) carries
`orderGe P (m-1)` into `orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` into `orderGe P 1`, hence
descends to the `k`-linear embedding `localStepTgt k P m ↪ κ(P)`.  Feeding it to

field `κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P` realised as the single-uniformizer-step valuation quotient

rational function `t` of order `1 - m` at `P` carries `orderGe P (m-1)` into
`orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` into `orderGe P 1`, hence descends to the
`k`-linear map `localStepTgt k P m → κ(P) = localStepTgt k P 1` between single-point
valuation quotients — the uniformizer-power shift of the fractional-ideal
filtration.  `k`-linearity is automatic: multiplication by a fixed element of
`K(X)` commutes with the `k`-action. -/

    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
    localStepTgt k P m →ₗ[k] localStepTgt k P 1 :=
  Submodule.mapQ _ _
    (LinearMap.restrict (LinearMap.mulLeft k t)
      (p := orderGeSub k P (m - 1)) (q := orderGeSub k P (1 - 1))
      (fun x hx => by
        rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hx
        rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub]
        rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with hx0 | hx0
        · exact Or.inl (by rw [hx0, mul_zero])
        · exact Or.inr (by
            rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hx0, hc]
            have := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx
            linarith)))
    (by
      intro x hx
      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, mem_orderGeSub] at hx
      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
        LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub]
      rcases eq_or_ne (x : X.functionField) 0 with hx0 | hx0
      · exact Or.inl (by rw [hx0, mul_zero])
      · exact Or.inr (by
          rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hx0, hc]

          linarith))

43	/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
44	one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
45	trivial. -/
46	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
47	    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
48	    classDeg K L = 0 := by
49	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
50	  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
51	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
52	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]
53	
54	/-! ## The relative degree -/
55	
56	/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
57	gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
58	`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
59	one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
60	field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/
61	noncomputable def relPicDeg (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
62	    Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ :=
63	  MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft
64	    (QuotientGroup.lift (picFromBase C (overSpec k K))
65	      (AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeRight (classDeg K))
66	      (fun L hL => by
67	        have h0 : classDeg K L = 0 := classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase hL
68	        rw [MonoidHom.mem_ker]
69	        change Multiplicative.ofAdd (classDeg K L) = 1
70	        rw [h0, ofAdd_zero]))
71	
72	/-- **The anchor of the relative degree**: on the class of `L`, the relative degree is
73	`classDeg K L`. -/
74	@[simp]
75	theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
76	    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
77	    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
78	  rfl
79	
80	/-- **E-iv-alg descended to the relative Picard group** (worksheet SB-5, second descent
81	gadget): the relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
82	map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions — the degree of a relative Picard class does not
83	depend on the field over which it is presented. -/
84	theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap {K₁ K₂ : Type u} [Field K₁] [Algebra k K₁] [Field K₂]
85	    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
86	    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
87	  induction x using relPic.ind with
88	  | mk L =>
89	    have h1 : relPicAlgMap C φ (relPicMk C (overSpec k K₁) L)
90	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k K₂)
91	          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
92	      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
93	    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
94	      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]
95	
96	end AlgebraicGeometry

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

/-- A **Weil divisor** on the curve `X`: a finitely supported `ℤ`-valued function on the
closed points, identified with the non-generic points of the irreducible scheme.  Carries the
`Finsupp` `AddCommGroup` structure and the pointwise partial order.  Independent of the base
field. -/
def CurveDivisor (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] : Type u :=
  {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ

namespace CurveDivisor

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]

noncomputable instance : AddCommGroup X.CurveDivisor :=
  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup ({x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ))

instance : PartialOrder X.CurveDivisor :=
  inferInstanceAs (PartialOrder ({x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ))

section Degree

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

attribute [local instance] Scheme.residueFieldOverModule

/-- The **degree** of a Weil divisor, weighted by the residue degrees over the base field:
`deg D = ∑ₓ Dₓ · [κ(x) : K]`. -/
noncomputable def deg (D : X.CurveDivisor) : ℤ :=
  D.sum fun x n => n * (X.residueDeg K x.1 : ℤ)

@[simp]
theorem deg_zero : deg K (0 : X.CurveDivisor) = 0 := by
  simp only [deg]
  exact Finsupp.sum_zero_index

/-- Degree is additive. -/
theorem deg_add (D D' : X.CurveDivisor) : deg K (D + D') = deg K D + deg K D' := by
  simp only [deg]
  refine Finsupp.sum_add_index' (fun _ => ?_) (fun _ b₁ b₂ => ?_)
  · simp
  · ring

/-- The degree of a single-point divisor `n · x` is `n · [κ(x) : K]`. -/
theorem deg_single (x : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) (n : ℤ) :
    deg K (Finsupp.single x n : X.CurveDivisor) = n * (X.residueDeg K x.1 : ℤ) := by
  simp only [deg]
  refine Finsupp.sum_single_index ?_
  simp

/-- Degree of a negated divisor. -/
theorem deg_neg (D : X.CurveDivisor) : deg K (-D) = -deg K D := by
  have h := deg_add K D (-D)
  rw [add_neg_cancel, deg_zero] at h
  linarith

end Degree

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.ChiLedger
7	
8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the multiplication isomorphism and class invariance
10	
11	This file supplies the **class-invariance layer** of the adelic χ-ledger: the
12	statement that all three numerical invariants of the ledger — `ℓ(D)`, `h¹(D)` and
13	`χ(D)` — depend only on the *linear-equivalence class* of `D`, together with the
14	elementary effective-witness dictionary that turns a nonzero global section into
15	an effective divisor in the same class.
16	
17	Everything here is **unconditional**: no gate class, no ledger exactness
18	hypothesis, no finiteness input.  The only mechanism is that multiplication by a
19	nonzero rational function `g ∈ K(X)^×` is a `k`-linear automorphism of `K(X)`
20	which carries the section subspace `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` *onto* `Γ(U, 𝒪(D − div g))`.
21	
22	## Main declarations
23	
24	* `Adelic.mul_mem_sectionOfDivisor` — the order computation
25	  `ord_P (g·f) = ord_P g + ord_P f`, in section-membership form: the single
26	  arithmetic fact behind everything else in this file.
27	* `Adelic.mulEquivFunctionField` — multiplication by `g ≠ 0` as a `k`-linear
28	  automorphism of `K(X)` (`k` a field of constants).
29	* `Adelic.map_sectionSub_mulEquiv` — `(Γ(U, 𝒪(D))).map (g·) = Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`
30	  whenever `D'(P) = D(P) − ord_P g` for every prime divisor `P`.
31	* `Adelic.sectionSubMulEquiv` — the resulting `k`-linear isomorphism
32	  `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`.
33	* `Adelic.ell_eq_of_shift`, `Adelic.h1dim_eq_of_shift`, `Adelic.chi_eq_of_shift`
34	  — `ℓ`, `h¹` and `χ` are invariant under the shift `D ↦ D − div g`.
35	* `Adelic.chi_eq_of_principal_shift`, `Adelic.chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`
36	  — the same statements spelled with `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal` and with the
37	  project's `LinearEquivalence` relation.
38	* `Adelic.exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem` — the effective-witness
39	  brick: a nonzero `f ∈ L(D)` exhibits `D + div f ≥ 0` in the class of `D`.
40	* `Adelic.one_le_ell_of_nonneg` — conversely an effective divisor has `ℓ ≥ 1`.
41	
42	## Provenance
43	
44	The mathematical content is the adelic (function-field) incarnation of the
45	sibling project's sheaf-theoretic `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` /
46	`chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` pair
47	(`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, `RiemannRoch/MulEquiv.lean` and
48	`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`).  **No code was ported**: that development is built on
49	a different substrate (`CurveDivisor` on closed points, `divisorSheaf`,
50	`Sheaf.chi`, `CechPic`), none of whose names exist in this project.  What is
51	reused is the *argument*: transport `χ` along multiplication by `g` and cancel in
52	the ledger.  Here the transport is elementary linear algebra on subspaces of
53	`K(X)`, which is why this file needs no finiteness or exactness input at all —
54	whereas the sheaf-theoretic form needs the χ-additivity machinery even to state
55	the transport.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	
60	universe u
61	
62	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
63	open scoped WithZero
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

68	/-! ## §1. The order arithmetic behind the multiplication isomorphism -/
69	
70	section Order
71	
72	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
73	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
74	
75	/-- **Multiplication by `g` shifts the section bound by `div g`.**  If
76	`D'(P) ≥ D(P) − ord_P g` at every prime divisor `P` of `U`, then multiplication
77	by `g ≠ 0` carries `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` into `Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`.
78	
79	This is `ord_P (g·f) = ord_P g + ord_P f` (`order_mul_of_ne_zero`) rearranged:
80	`ord_P (g·f) ≥ ord_P g − D(P) ≥ −D'(P)`.  Stated with an inequality rather than
81	an equality on `D'` so that the same lemma serves both directions of the
82	isomorphism (apply it to `g⁻¹` for the inverse). -/
83	theorem mul_mem_sectionOfDivisor {U : X.Opens} {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
84	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
85	    (hD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
86	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g ≤
87	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)
88	    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D) :
89	    g * f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D' := by
90	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
91	  · simp
92	  refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
93	  have hord := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf P hP
94	  rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P hg hf0]
95	  have := hD' P hP
96	  linarith
97	
98	end Order
99	
100	/-! ## §2. Multiplication by `g` as a `k`-linear automorphism -/
101	
102	section MulEquiv
103	
104	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
105	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
106	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
107	
108	/-- **Multiplication by a nonzero rational function, as a `k`-linear
109	automorphism of `K(X)`.**  The inverse is multiplication by `g⁻¹`.  `k`-linearity
110	is automatic: multiplication by a fixed element of `K(X)` commutes with the
111	`k`-action. -/
112	noncomputable def mulEquivFunctionField (g : X.functionField) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
113	    X.functionField ≃ₗ[k] X.functionField :=
114	  LinearEquiv.ofLinear (LinearMap.mulLeft k g) (LinearMap.mulLeft k g⁻¹)
115	    (by ext x; simp [mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hg])
116	    (by ext x; simp [inv_mul_cancel_left₀ hg])
117	
118	omit [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [X.IsRegularInCodimensionOne] [IsConstantField k X] in
119	@[simp] theorem mulEquivFunctionField_apply (g : X.functionField) (hg : g ≠ 0)
120	    (f : X.functionField) : mulEquivFunctionField k g hg f = g * f := rfl

namespace DivFamily

variable {π : X ⟶ S}

/-- The **fibre degree** of a family of relative effective divisors
`x : DivFamily π T` at a point `t : T` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`):

  `deg D_t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,

the `κ(t)`-dimension of the global sections of the restriction of the divisor
structure sheaf `F = O_D` to the scheme-theoretic fibre `(X_T)_t`.  This is
the pointwise shadow of "rank of the finite-flat pushforward `q_* O_D`" (equal
to it whenever the pushforward exists as a locally free module, i.e. in the
relative-curve regime once the B3 engine lands; see the module docstring
audit).  `Module.finrank` junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case. -/
noncomputable def fiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : ℕ :=
  letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
    ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F)
  Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
    Γ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F, ⊤)

/-- **The fibre degree is well defined on divisor classes**: equivalent
families (`DivFamily.Rel`, i.e. same divisor `ker q = ker q'`) have equal
fibre degrees — the target isomorphism restricts to each fibre and transports
the section dimension. -/
theorem Rel.fiberDeg_eq {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : x.fiberDeg t = y.fiberDeg t := by
  obtain ⟨f, -⟩ := h
  exact finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T.hom) t
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).mapIso f)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- Heartbeat headroom: instantiating the Γ-fibre base-change core provisions
-- pullback/pushforward and field instances under binders, as in the sibling
-- engines of `QuotFunctorDef`.
/-- **The fibre degree is stable under base change** (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`;
Kleiman §3, functoriality of `Div`): for `ψ : T' ⟶ T` and `t' : T'` over
`t := ψ(t')`, the fibre degree of the pulled-back family at `t'` equals the
fibre degree of `x` at `t`.

Route (all inputs axiom-clean): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is the base
change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t` along `Spec κ(t') → Spec κ(t)`
(`Scheme.isPullback_fiberBaseChange`, the `quotBaseSquare`/residue-field
pasting); the two fibre restrictions of `F` are matched by pseudofunctor
coherence (`Scheme.pullbackSquareIso`); proper support of `F/T` restricts to
the fibre (`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback` on Mathlib's fibre
square); and the twist-free Γ-fibre flat base-change core
`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean` — support descent `G ≅ i_* i^* G` + the
CLOSED 02KE heart) transports the dimension across the residue extension.
No tensor operations enter, so — unlike the twisted engine
`hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` — this consumes no sorried leaf. -/
theorem fiberDeg_pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) (x : DivFamily π T)
    (t' : (T'.left : Scheme.{u})) :
    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).fiberDeg t' = x.fiberDeg (ψ.left.base t') := by

  haveI : ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule (ψ.left.base t') x.F).IsQuasicoherent :=
    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom _ x.F hFqc
  have hpsFt : Modules.HasProperSupport
